chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim Al-Ju'fi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the chamber of Umm Salma (peace be upon her) and smelled a good aroma, so he said: "Has Al-Hawla come to you?"' She said: 'It is she. She is complaining about her husband.' So Al-Hawla came out to him and said: 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! My husband has turned away from me.' He said: 'Increase it (the perfume), O Hawla.' She said: 'I have not left any good perfume that I do not use it for him, and he turns away from me.' He said: 'But if only he knew what is for him with his facing towards you.' She said: 'And what is for him with facing towards me?' He said: 'Indeed, when he faces you, two angels encircle him, so he is like the striker of his sword in the Way of Allah. And when he copulates, the sins fall off from him as the leaves of the tree fall. And when he bathes, he is stripped of the sins.'

key_terms.الْحَوْلَاءُ: Al-Hawla (a proper name, likely a servant or attendant of Umm Salma)
key_terms.وَورَقُ الشَّجَرِ: And the leaves of the tree

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for marital intimacy in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Umm Salma?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) encourages Umm Salma to use perfume to rekindle her husband's affection, illustrating the Shia emphasis on *zawjiyyah* (marital companionship) as a form of worship rather than mere physical act. He draws a parallel between marital intimacy and *jihad*, noting that sexual union results in the shedding of sins like falling leaves, while subsequent ritual bathing (*ghusl*) provides further purification. This narrative underscores the spiritual merit of maintaining marital harmony and counters the notion of ascetic neglect of conjugal duties.
